expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: trialing has trialEndsAt; active has renewsAt; past_due has retryCount/gracePeriodEndsAt/failedAt; canceled has canceledAt/cancellation

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: Recommends it in prose ('Pair every switch with an `assertNever(x: never)` default arm') but does not show working code that includes/uses it

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Uses `readonly` on all fields to enforce single-path mutation and explicitly recommends `transition()` function as 'the only writer'

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Discusses two things the union 'does not give you' and one thing it stops ('describing a nonsense subscription'), but does not systematically enumerate misuses prevented

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Implicitly addresses via discriminated union pattern without the optional-field alternative
